Synopsis:
WPP, the UK's largest advertising group, is cutting up to 1,000 additional jobs by year-end as part of an accelerating restructuring under new CEO Cindy Rose. Since early 2025, WPP has shed ~11,000 roles (headcount now ~97,388). The restructuring consolidates creative agencies under a "WPP Creative" umbrella, leverages AI, and targets a return to growth in 2027. The company is also divesting non-core assets and reducing its property footprint, responding to competitive pressure from rivals like Publicis and the broader disruption of AI in the advertising industry.
